log: Initial commit
Update error text
Work in progress - core AI `Strategy` rewrite.

The standard workflow from civ-clone/web-renderer#66: Node 22, pnpm with no lock file and web-renderer's settings, and it runs the tests. prettier:check now has --check, so it fails on unformatted files instead of printing them.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.
StrategyAIClient.takeTurn is rewritten so that SimpleAIClient can extend it without changing play:
BeforeTurn and AfterTurn actions, offered once per turn to every Strategy that handles them (StrategyRegistry.attemptAll).

Mandatory actions are taken one at a time, with exactly one hasMandatoryActions() and one mandatoryAction() call per action, the same calls in the same order as SimpleAIClient.takeTurn. Each builds PlayerActions and so uses DataObject ids, and nothing else lists the player's actions.

The turn ends at the first action no Strategy handles, after an unhandledAction hook. That is how a turn ends normally: the engine's EndTurn is offered once nothing else is mandatory, and nothing handles it. Before, EndTurn kept the loop running forever, or threw UnhandledAction.
A thrown error goes to actionFailed, which can carry on, end the turn, or rethrow (the default). SimpleAIClient will use it to skip a broken unit.
actionLimit (1,000) and actionLimitReached replace the 10,000-action UnhandledAction throw, and are checked where SimpleAIClient checks its loopCheck, so it can reproduce that exactly.
Non-mandatory actions are no longer offered (they were, with Promise.all), and takeTurn no longer recurses. Offering them will be added deliberately later, because it changes play.
The RNG defaults to core-random's seeded instance, not Math.random, and the fields are TypeScript private rather than #private.
chooseFromList awaits the registry and only uses a Strategy's answer if it called choose(); otherwise it falls back to Client's random pick, unchanged.
UnhandledAction is removed, as nothing throws it now. The package gets its first tests, and depends on core-strategy 0.1.6 for the async registry.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.
CI installs with pnpm and no lock file, and nothing reads this one.
Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#66.

takeTurn's try also wrapped actionLimit, actionLimitReached and unhandledAction, so a subclass whose actionFailed carries on could swallow a failing limit hook and loop past the guard forever. Only registry.attempt is inside the try now; a throw from a hook fails the turn. The order of calls, including exactly one hasMandatoryActions() and one mandatoryAction() per action, is unchanged.

chooseFromList used registry.attempt, which only says that some strategy returned true, while the choice could have been made by an earlier strategy that returned false. It now goes through registry.ordered itself, resets the Data (new Data.reset()) before each strategy, and uses the value only when that same strategy both chose and returned true. Otherwise it falls back to Client's random pick as before.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.
The same steps as core-strategy's workflow: tsc --build --force and prettier:format, then fail if either changed a tracked file, before the tests run against the committed .js.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

`git diff --exit-code` only sees tracked files, so a new module whose `.js` was never added passed, and the published package would omit it. The check now fails on modified or untracked `.js`, `.d.ts` and `.js.map`, listing them, and ignores everything else, such as the lock file the install writes.
Same change as civ-clone/core-random#1. Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#66.

The registries, engine and random number generator the constructor receives are now one `Dependencies` bag (lib/Dependencies.ts), with no player in it. The seven target lists and the three per-unit maps are one `Memory` object (lib/Memory.ts) owned by the client, holding the same arrays and maps for the same lifetimes. The old field names stay as private getters, since the tests reach in for `_citiesToLiberate`.
No change in play. Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

`shouldAttack`, `movesBetween` and `carriersFor` are generic modules. Aircraft fuel and whether an aircraft can get home (lib/Civ1/aircraft.ts) and the terrain judgements for cities, irrigation, mines and roads (lib/Civ1/terrain.ts) are Civ1 modules. Each takes the dependency bag and the player instead of reading the client.
No change in play. Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

`preProcessTurn` now delegates to three generic modules: the target survey (lib/Turn/surveyTargets.ts), the pass over the player's cities that assigns workers and notes undefended ones (lib/Turn/reviewCities.ts), and waking aircraft aboard carriers (lib/Turn/wakeCarrierAircraft.ts). The revolution to Monarchy that starts `takeTurn` is lib/Civ1/government.ts.

Where a generic module needs a Civ1 judgement (a good city site, which tiles citizens work, whether a unit is an aircraft) it asks a `Knowledge` (lib/Knowledge.ts), which lib/Civ1/knowledge.ts supplies.
The survey's three missing `!`s are kept and marked. No change in play. Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

Opening and running a negotiation with neighbouring players (lib/Diplomacy/negotiate.ts) and the answer chosen at each step (lib/Diplomacy/chooseNegotiationStep.ts) are generic modules. The awaits, the 500 ms race and the 20 ms sleep are where they were, and `chooseFromList` still settles in the same number of ticks.
No change in play. Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

`moveUnit` (lib/Unit/moveUnit.ts: follow the path, else take the best-scored step) and `scoreUnitMove` (lib/Unit/scoreUnitMove.ts) are generic modules, along with standing a unit down (lib/Unit/orders.ts) and the by-name action lookup (lib/actionLookup.ts). The action and unit type classes now come from library-unit, which civ1-unit re-exports, so they are the same classes.

The random tie-break stays inside the sort comparator. The client's `moveUnit` hands back the module's promise without an extra `async`, so awaiting it takes the same ticks. No change in play. Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

A unit's turn is now generic modules run in the old order: aircraft wait for carriers (lib/Unit/waitForCarrier.ts), then lib/Unit/takeUnitTurn.ts seeds the move history and runs transport unloading, a worker's tile work, garrisoning, mission assignment and the move executor. Tile work and mission assignment still fall through into the move executor.

Mission assignment (lib/Unit/assignMission.ts) is six first-match missions in priority order: undefended city, liberate, enemy units, enemy cities, explore land, explore sea. A unit that qualifies for one tries no other, even with no path, and each sorts the same list in place (or a filtered copy) as before.
`takeUnitTurn` returns the move executor's promise, or `null` when the unit acted without moving, so `takeTurn` awaits exactly where it used to. No change in play. Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

What a city builds (lib/Civ1/buildItemInCity.ts) and which government to take after Anarchy (added to lib/Civ1/government.ts) are Civ1 modules. The random research pick (lib/Science/chooseResearch.ts) is generic.

City production still draws its random pick on every call, before it knows whether it'll use it. Two defects are kept and marked: the Wonder choice is always replaced by the random pick, and the count of fortified units counts every unit. No change in play. Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

`cityLost` (lib/Events/cityLost.ts) and `unitDestroyed` (lib/Events/unitDestroyed.ts) are generic modules. `unitDestroyed` is handed the client's city production to run. Both still act on the same target board during other players' turns.
Kept and marked: `cityLost` targets the player's own cities, and `unitDestroyed` ignores who destroyed the unit. No change in play. Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.
Sorts the module imports and imports the negotiation module for its `ChoiceMetaDataMap` entry, so the declaration keeps it for anyone reading SimpleAIClient.d.ts. Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.
docs: fix typos and grammar in comments

`lib/MemoryRegistry.ts` hands out one `Memory` per player, created on first use and held in a `WeakMap`. It sits in the dependency bag, so the client and the strategies coming next reach the same arrays and maps. The client's `cityLost`, `unitDestroyed` and private getters read it through `memory()`. `createDependencies` fills the bag from the module singletons, with any of them replaced.
No change in play. Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

Each concern in `lib/` gets a stateless `core-strategy` `Strategy` in `Strategies/`. Each takes the dependency bag and the ruleset's `Knowledge`, gets the player from the action and narrows `handles` to what it deals with. Generic strategies are grouped by concern (`Turn/`, `Unit/`, `Science/`, `Diplomacy/`) and Civ1 ones are in `Strategies/Civ1/`.

`registerStrategies.ts` builds the pack in today's decision order (`createStrategies`) and registers it into `game.strategies`, including `defaultGame` from `index.ts`, as `registerRules` does. It registers no `Priority` rules. The unit strategies share one per-action context (`Strategies/lib/unitTurnContextFor.ts`), so each unit's turn still reads its actions and seeds its move history once. `takeUnitTurn` builds the same context through `lib/Unit/unitTurnContext.ts`.

`SimpleAIClient` doesn't use the pack yet, so nothing plays differently. Depends on `@civ-clone/core-strategy@^0.1.6` and `@civ-clone/core-strategy-ai-client@^0.1.2`, neither published yet. Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

`SimpleAIClient` keeps its name, its positional constructor and defaults, its public methods and the `Rules/` hooks. It gains an optional trailing `strategyRegistry`, defaulting to the game-wide registry that `registerStrategies` fills. The turn loop is now `StrategyAIClient`'s: `BeforeTurn`, then one mandatory action at a time, then `AfterTurn`. `chooseFromList` is its `ChooseFromList` adapter, and the base `Client` pick is the fallback. The Civ1 client overrides only the hooks, which reproduce today's handling: `actionFailed` skips a failed unit and rethrows anything else, `actionLimitReached` logs the 1,000-action diagnostics and gives `NoOrders`, and `unhandledAction` logs anything that isn't `EndTurn`.
The test setup builds a `StrategyRegistry` over the same registries it hands the client. No assertion changes.

Conformance is identical at 50 and 150 turns (checksums, RNG draws, state and DTO). test:load's saved-game hash moves from 6cb2a96f to 650ca666, because the suite saves synchronously inside `turn:start`, part-way into the first player's turn, and `StrategyAIClient` awaits sooner than the old loop did. The old client with one `await` added at the start of `takeTurn` saves 650ca666 too. Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

`base-unit-type-naval-transport` was declared but never imported. `core-city-improvement` is imported only by the tests, so it moves to devDependencies. `lib/Unit/takeUnitTurn.ts` is unused now that the unit strategies run its steps, and its context is `lib/Unit/unitTurnContext.ts`.
docs: describe the strategy pack and how a plugin extends or overrides it
docs: say the pack is registered by importing the package index

`StrategyAIClient` is moving `actionLimitReached` outside its `try`, so a throw from the hook will fail the turn instead of reaching `actionFailed`. The override now catches anything its diagnostics or `NoOrders` throw: a unit is skipped, as `actionFailed` does, and anything else fails the turn. It works the same with the current base class and the new one.

This differs from the old loop in one case only: when the 1,000-action guard trips and `NoOrders` also throws for a unit, the old loop carried on and the turn now ends. Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

localChanges: A game that was loaded from a save and then saved again now carries on with the same random events as a game that was never interrupted (closes #17).

log: `restore(seed, calls)` moved the generator onto `seed`'s stream but left `seed()` returning the seed it was constructed with. The default instance is constructed from `Date.now()`, so any process that took control with `restore` and then saved recorded a clock value as the seed: loading that file resumed a different stream at the right draw count.

This made the played-on hash of web-renderer's load suite vary between runs (six values over 30 runs, one per advance a single random research pick could land on), and affects any game in the browser that is loaded and then saved again. With the fix the loaded game matches uninterrupted play on every run (civ-clone/web-renderer#17).

Adds the standard `build-on-push.yml` (Node 22, pnpm, no lock file), with the compile step that fails when the committed `.js` is stale, and makes `prettier:check` actually check (civ-clone/web-renderer#66).
Nothing installs from it: CI resolves with pnpm and no lock file, as a consumer does (civ-clone/web-renderer#66).

`restore` normalised the seed it reports (`>>> 0`) but computed the state from the raw value, so after restoring a negative or fractional seed the generator was not at the position `seed()` and `calls()` describe, and a generator restored from them drew differently. The state is now computed from the normalised seed, as `createRng` does.

`git diff --exit-code` only sees tracked files, so a new module whose `.js` was never added passed, and the published package would omit it. The check now fails on modified or untracked `.js`, `.d.ts` and `.js.map`, listing them, and ignores everything else, such as the lock file the install writes.

The standard workflow from civ-clone/web-renderer#66: Node 22, pnpm with no lock file and web-renderer's settings. prettier:check now has --check, so it fails on unformatted files instead of printing them.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

StrategyRegistry.attempt broke ties between equal priorities with an RNG draw inside the sort comparator. How many numbers that drew depended on the sort, and every draw moved the game's seeded sequence, so it could not be used without changing play. It also recomputed priorities on every comparison, and `a - b` is NaN when both are Infinity (no Priority rule applies).

Now each Strategy's priority is computed once, ties go to registration order, and nothing is random. The RNG constructor argument is still accepted, for core-game's `new StrategyRegistry(rng)`, but not used, so core-random is no longer a dependency.
Strategy.attempt may return a Promise<boolean>. StrategyRegistry.attempt resolves a Promise<boolean> and awaits each attempt before the next, stopping at the first true.
Strategy.handles(action), default true, is a cheap filter checked before any Priority rule is evaluated or attempt is called.
StrategyRegistry.attemptAll(action) runs every handling Strategy in the same order, whatever each returns, for per-turn hooks that several plugins contribute to.

Nothing in the game calls StrategyRegistry.attempt yet. Strategy.test.ts's duplicates of the registry tests are removed; it used `spy` without `use(spies)` and only passed because StrategyRegistry.test.ts, loaded in the same run, calls it.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

getByKey scanned every note, and register and replace call it too. It now reads an EntityRegistry.index keyed on the note's key, which is fixed for the note's lifetime (replace swaps notes rather than re-keying one). Requires core-registry 0.1.3, the first version with index().

A save restores notes the same way: core-save-game's hydrate fills each entity before registering it into game.strategyNotes, so register files it under its key. There is a test that restores a note that way.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

It accepts anything with an id(), but only called it on a DataObject and used toString() on everything else, which gave "[object Object]" for, say, a plain object with an id(). Every current caller passes DataObjects or strings, so no existing key changes.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

The README still described Routines. It now covers handles, async attempt, attempt and attemptAll, and the contract: strategies are game-wide and stateless, take the player from action.player(), keep memory in notes keyed by player and unit, and can be run directly for one unit or city, e.g. to automate a human player's unit.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#66.

The example used RuleRegistry, TraitRegistry, Leader, Trait and the registry instances without importing them. Every library identifier is imported now, and the plugin-specific placeholders (MyAction, MyTrait, doSomethingWith) are listed as such.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

It lists the strategies that handle an action, in the order attempt tries them. A caller that needs to know which strategy produced a result, such as StrategyAIClient.chooseFromList attributing a choice to the strategy that accepted it, iterates them itself.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

The tests load the committed .js, so CI could pass on source that no longer type-checks, or whose compiled output was never rebuilt. CI now compiles with tsc --build --force and runs prettier:format, then fails if either changed a tracked file. --force because a fresh checkout's timestamps can make tsc --build treat the committed output as up to date and skip the compile.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#153.

localChanges: A unit that still has moves left now stays selected after it moves. Before, another unit could be selected, the map jumped to it, and your next key press moved the wrong unit (closes #189).

log: The capital lookup scanned the registry without a destroyed() check, so a Palace destroyed on capture counted as the capturer's (or re-taker's) capital, zeroing corruption (civ-clone/web-renderer#186). Corruption distance now uses civ1-world's civ1Distance rather than the straight-line Tile#distanceFrom (civ-clone/web-renderer#180); the far city in the corruption table moves from 28.28 to 30.

Replaces the Node 12 / yarn workflow with the standard one (Node 22, pnpm, no lock file, so it tests what a consumer resolves). Removes yarn.lock, which pinned civ1-world to a commit without lib/civ1Distance, and .yarnrc.yml. prettier:check now has --check, and the test-only import is declared.

A Created rule on Palace destroys the player's other live Palaces, so the capital moves to the new city (civ-clone/web-renderer#187). Hydrating a save doesn't run constructors, so loading is unaffected. The corruption table follows civ1-city's switch to Civ1's distance (#180).

Replaces the Node 12 / yarn workflow with the standard one (Node 22, pnpm, no lock file, so it tests what a consumer resolves). Removes yarn.lock, which pinned civ1-world to a commit without lib/civ1Distance, and .yarnrc.yml. prettier:check now has --check, and the test-only import is declared.

max(dx, dy) + floor(min(dx, dy) / 2), wrapping on x only, as v474.05's GetShortestDistance. For corruption now (civ-clone/web-renderer#180), and trade routes, incite cost and discontent later (#57, #58, #123). Tile#distanceFrom stays the engine's general straight-line measure.
Replaces the Node 12 / yarn workflow with the standard one (Node 22, pnpm, no lock file) and removes yarn.lock and .yarnrc.yml. prettier:check now has --check.

localChanges: Losing your capital now raises corruption in your remaining cities, as in Civ1. A Palace you captured in someone else's capital no longer counts as yours, which could leave every one of your cities with no corruption at all (closes #186).
Building a Palace in another city now moves your capital there: the old Palace is removed, and corruption is measured from the new one (closes #187).
Distance to your capital is now measured as in Civ1, where a diagonal step counts about one and a half, so corruption in distant cities matches the original (closes #180).
chore: update simple-ai-client

log: `City#capture` processes `Captured` with `(city, capturingPlayer, previousOwner)`, as `civ1-player`'s rule reads it, but this rule named the arguments `(city, player, capturingPlayer)`. The criterion therefore checked the capturer's client and the effect called `cityLost` on it, so the capturer queued its own new city in `_citiesToLiberate` and the losing AI never tried to retake it.
Adds tests/captured.test.ts, which fails without the fix.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#127.

localChanges: When a computer player loses a city to capture, it now sends units to take it back. Before, the civilization that captured the city was the one told it had been lost, so it set off to "liberate" its own conquest (closes #127).
chore: update civ1-unit

log: Nothing touched the `TransportRegistry` when a unit was destroyed, so every way of losing a transport other than combat outside a city (`LostAtSea`, `Disband`, an unsupported unit, a home city captured or destroyed) left its cargo alive, `Stowed`, on a transport that no longer existed. Combat destroyed the cargo through the stack rule but left the manifests registered, and saved.
Two `Destroyed` rules, which every path goes through:
`unit/destroyed/lose-cargo`: unregisters the transport's manifests. On `Water` the cargo is destroyed, crediting the same player; on land (a city) it is left there, no longer `Stowed`.
`unit/destroyed/leave-transport`: a destroyed unit that is aboard something is unregistered from it.
`getRules` takes the `TransportRegistry` as a new trailing parameter.
civ-clone/web-renderer#104

`Stowed` never clears itself, so cargo destroyed with its transport, or by the stack rule before it, stayed `Stowed` with no manifest behind it. Both rules now go through one `leaveTransport`, which unregisters the manifest and clears `Stowed`.
civ-clone/web-renderer#104

localChanges: When a ship or Carrier is lost at sea, the units aboard are lost with it, whether it sank in a storm, was disbanded, or was lost because its home city was captured or could no longer support it. Before, they were left stranded at sea, still aboard a ship that no longer existed (closes #104).
When a ship or Carrier is lost in one of your cities, the units aboard now stay in the city and can be moved again.
chore: update civ1-city

log: `release-occupied-worked-tile` only fired when the unit ended its step with no moves left, so a unit that stopped with moves in hand (then fortified, slept or waited) left the city working the tile underneath it. It now fires on every move onto a tile worked by another player's city, and never releases a city's centre (the old rule did, for a unit moving onto it with no moves left).

A new `civ1-city:player/turn-start/release-occupied-worked-tiles` runs before the city yields are processed and releases any worked tile with another player's unit on it, which also covers loaded games and anything that put a unit there without a `Moved` rule.
civ-clone/web-renderer#139

The turn-start case now also puts an enemy unit on the city centre and the city's own unit on a worked tile, and checks both `WorkedTile`s survive by identity (a released tile the city takes straight back looks the same by `Tile`). A `High` `TurnStart` observer, standing in for civ1-player's `process-city-yields`, checks the occupied tile is already released when it runs.

localChanges: Your cities no longer work a tile while another civilization's unit stands on it, even if the unit stops there with moves left, fortifies or sleeps. The citizen moves to the best free tile, or becomes an Entertainer if none is free. Once the unit leaves, you can pick the tile again on the city screen (closes #139).

After you end your turn, the map now says "Waiting for the other civilizations…" until your next turn is ready. Until then no unit blinks as if it could still move, and the End Turn button stays hidden. Before, the game looked ready but ignored your keys (#130).
The new turn now arrives all at once: the turn, year and treasury update together, before that turn's messages such as "Building complete" (#130).
The map keeps up better while the other civilizations move, instead of freezing and flashing in large games (closes #61).
chore: update core-world-path, core-world-generator, base-unit-action-goto, civ1-unit and simple-world-path

log: `moveAlongPath` shifted the next tile off the path before trying the move. A unit short of the moves a tile costs only gets there by chance (civ1-unit's `not-enough-moves`), so when the attempt failed the unit stayed put, the tile was gone, and the rest of the path started somewhere the unit wasn't. From then on nothing was adjacent: each turn dropped another tile, and the journey "finished" wherever the unit happened to be.

The tile is now only shifted once the unit is on it, so a failed attempt is retried the next turn. When no `Move` onto the next tile exists at all (an enemy unit on it, say), the journey ends straight away and the unit is handed back. Before, that happened a tile a turn, by the same draining. `passingThrough` is now `path.length > 1`, because the target is still in `path` when it's checked.

Adds the package's first tests: a failed move is retried the next turn, a path is followed to its end, and a blocked path ends the journey. Two of the three fail on the previous code. Also brings CI up to the standard setup: pnpm on Node 22, `prettier --check`, the test step on, and test dependencies declared.
Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#40, civ-clone/web-renderer#66.

`civ1-unit:unit/expected-movement-cost/shortfall` answers core-world-path's `ExpectedMovementCost`. With full moves `m`, a step costing `c > m` gets the unit in with a chance of `min(1, m / (c × 0.5))` per turn, and each attempt spends the turn (`not-enough-moves`). So on average the step is worth `max(m, c × 0.5)`: one turn while success is certain, and `1 / chance` turns after that. A Warrior prices mountains at 1.5 and hills at 1.

The 0.5 is now `shortfallFactor`, exported from `validateMove.ts` and used by both rules, so the chance and its price can't drift apart. The tests check the price against `validateMove`'s own outcomes across every draw.
Needs core-world-path 0.1.2, which adds the rule type.
Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#40.

With `directNeighbours = false`, `se` was computed from `(x + 1, y)`, so the eight-neighbour list held the east tile twice and never the south-east one. No live caller asks for all eight, so no generated map changes.

Adds the package's first tests (every neighbour, in order, for a middle tile, the corners and each wrap seam) and brings CI up to the standard setup: pnpm on Node 22, `prettier --check`, and the test step switched on.
Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#103, civ-clone/web-renderer#66.

CI installs prettier 2.8.8, which parenthesises `(typeof Terrain)[]`. With `prettier:check` now actually checking (`--check`), these two files failed the build. They were never checked before, because the old script ran without `--check`.

A `Rule<[Unit, movementCost, movement], number>` that says what a step is worth to a route, on average, when it costs more than the unit's whole turn. That's when entering the tile can take more than one attempt. The rules that decide whether such a move succeeds are a ruleset's own (civ1-unit's `not-enough-moves`), so the price belongs beside them and not in a path finder. A path finder asks this only for those steps, and passes `movement` in because working it out is a yield calculation.
Also brings CI up to the standard setup: pnpm on Node 22, `prettier --check`, and `yarn.lock` removed.
Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#40, civ-clone/web-renderer#66.

Since 8878cb8, `generate()` ran the `MovementCost` rules for every neighbour but gave each step a cost of 1, so the search was breadth-first by step count, stopped at the first route within 110% of the straight-line distance, and never preferred a road or railroad. `Path#movementCost()` was the step count.

`generate()` is now a uniform-cost search: a binary heap of open nodes and a `Map` of the best node per tile, in place of the linear `_heap.some` and `_seen.includes` scans. Each step costs what the `MovementCost` rules say, capped at the unit's movement per turn (a one-move unit spends a turn entering hills just as it does grassland, via `not-enough-moves`), and 1 if no rule answers, as before. Ties go to fewer steps, so zero-cost rail still gives the shortest route. There is no distance heuristic, because rail costs 0. The search stops when the goal leaves the heap. `Node` gains `totalCost` and `steps`, and `movementCost()` is now the real total.
A 150-turn headless game in web-renderer (`tools/bench.js`) went from 18.5s to 14.6s.

Tests: road over mountains, rail over road, fewest steps on a cost tie, and the one-move cap for hills against a three-move unit. The duplicate `unitYield` registration is removed, because core-rule now rejects duplicate rule ids, which stopped the suite from running. CI moves to the standard setup: pnpm on Node 22, `prettier --check`, `yarn.lock` and `.yarnrc.yml` removed, and the imports that were missing from `package.json` declared.
Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#40, civ-clone/web-renderer#66.

A step that costs more than the unit's whole turn can take more than one attempt (civ1-unit's `not-enough-moves` lets it in by chance). Capping it at a turn priced a Warrior's mountains like grassland, although it gets in only 2 times in 3. For those steps the path finder now asks core-world-path's `ExpectedMovementCost` rules, passing `(unit, movementCost, movement)`. With no rule it still costs a turn.
It's asked only for those steps, and `movement` is passed rather than recalculated: asking on every step was no slower in a 150-turn bench, but recalculating `unit.movement()` in the rule added 8s.
Tests: a priced rule sends a Warrior around five mountains (8 steps at 1 each) rather than across them (5 × 1.5 + 1), and is only asked about the mountains. Without the rule, it goes straight across.
Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#40.

The tie-break compared `totalCost` exactly. Six road steps (6 × 1/3) sum to 1.9999999999999998, so a six-step road loop beat two grassland steps that cost exactly 2, contrary to "fewer steps wins ties". Costs within 1e-9 of each other now count as equal. Found by Copilot's review.
Test: from (1, 1) to (3, 1), two grassland steps are chosen over a six-step road loop of the same cost. It fails before this change.
Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#40.

cb340cd compared costs with a 1e-9 tolerance. That isn't transitive: with (cost, steps) A = (2, 3), B = (2 + 0.75e-9, 2), C = (2 + 1.5e-9, 1), it says B < A, C < B and A < C, and a binary heap needs a strict weak order, so it could pop the wrong node first. Each node now carries `costKey`, its total cost rounded to millionths, and nodes compare by `(costKey, steps)`, which is transitive. Six road steps (1.9999999999999998) and 2 still share a key, so the float-tie test still holds. Found by Copilot's review.
Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#40.

localChanges: A unit on GoTo that fails to get into mountains, or any tile it hasn't the moves for, now tries again the next turn. Before, it lost its route and stopped somewhere along the way (#40).
When choosing a route, units now allow for those failed attempts, so a unit with one move a turn will often go around a mountain range rather than over it.

Units sent with GoTo, and the computer players' units, now choose the route that gets them there soonest, following roads and railroads even when that's a longer way round. They no longer walk around hills or forest that would take them no longer to cross (#40).

In a big game, every message about one of your cities, and every update after a move, carried the whole map you had explored along with it. So the start of a turn could hang for several seconds, with the map flickering, the old turn still showing and keypresses ignored. Those messages now carry only what they're about. On a turn-265 save, one message went from 2 MB to 44 KB, and the updates for a whole turn from about 5 MB to 1.6 MB (#130).
Cruisers, Battleships, Submarines, Carriers, Transports, Nuclear, Diplomats and Caravans no longer have a light-blue line down their right-hand side and along the bottom (closes #12).
If you've already imported your assets, import them again from the main menu with "Replace existing assets?" ticked to get the fixed sprites.

log: The workflow is the standard one the other engine repos use (Node 22, pnpm, no lock file), `prettier:check` now actually checks, and `npm test` runs mocha over `tests/`, which the next commit starts filling.

`takeByCivilization` and friends shuffled the pool with `sort()` and a random comparator. The number of draws that makes depends on the size of the pool, so any difference in the pool — a loaded game's, for one — sent the rest of the random stream somewhere else, and the pick was not uniform. Each pick is now one draw, used as an index, and an empty pool draws nothing.

`takeByCivilization` also skips capital names now, and `takeCapitalByCivilization` picks among capital names only. A capital name could previously be drawn for an ordinary city whenever it was still in the pool, which after a load it always is (civ-clone/web-renderer#120).
The pool is filled by plugin imports, so a save does not carry it, and a loaded game had every name back in it: the next city could be named after the capital (civ-clone/web-renderer#120).

`taken()` lists every name handed out, in order, and `counter()` is the next `City #n`. `restore(taken, counter)` takes those names out of a freshly filled pool again. A record matches on its name and its civilization, since names repeat between civilizations (there's an English Athens as well as the Greek one), falling back to the same name in the unassociated pool. It replaces `taken()` rather than adding to it, and keeps records that match nothing, so a restore is idempotent and saving again writes the same list.

Review on #1. `restore()` fell back to the unassociated pool for any record whose own civilization's entry was gone, so restoring the same list twice, or into a pool this game had already drawn from, took the unassociated copy of a shared name as well. And a record matched through that fallback was kept as the unassociated entry, so saving again wrote `civilization: null`.
A record already in `taken()` is now left alone rather than matched against the pool, and `taken()` keeps each record as given.
The city name pool is a definition registry, so a loaded game had every name back in it, and the next city founded could be named after the capital (civ-clone/web-renderer#120).

A save now records `cityNames: { taken, counter }`: each name handed out, with its civilization's type name (names repeat between civilizations), and the next `City #n`. `hydrate` resolves the civilizations through `game.classes`, refusing one it cannot, and calls `cityNames.restore()`, which leaves the pool as the saved game had it.

The field is optional, so the format stays 2. A file without it falls back to the names of the cities it holds, each matched against its owner's civilization, and the counter resumes after the highest `City #n`. The names of cities destroyed before such a save can't be recovered.
Needs @civ-clone/core-civilization with `CityNameRegistry#taken`, `#counter` and `#restore`; the range is raised once that's published.
Require core-civilization 0.1.7, which records the city names handed out

Review on #3. The fallback for files without `cityNames` matched each city against its current owner's civilization, but a captured city keeps the name it was founded with: a Greek Sparta held by England left the Greek Sparta in the pool to be handed out again. It now uses `originalPlayer()` where the city has one. Also corrects the pass count in `hydrate`'s comment, which is seven now.

They are now `PendingEffect`s in `game.pendingEffects`, the same way `civ1-government` records a revolution under way: `civ1-city-happiness:civil-disorder` and `civ1-city-happiness:leader-celebration`, each targeting the `City`. Discharging one emits `city:order-restored` or `city:leader-celebration-ended`. `pendingEffects` is already a `state` slot and `PendingEffect` already saves generically, so the save format doesn't change, and older saves load as before, with no statuses recorded.

log: `Revolution` used to be applied by the client, which set the chosen government straight away. Now:

`lib/revolution.ts` owns the change. `revolution()` puts the player into Anarchy for as many turns as the new `AnarchyDuration` rules allow (the shortest answer wins; the default is 1-4, Rome on 640K a Day p18-19) and records the choice it owes as a `PendingEffect` targeting the `PlayerGovernment`, with the turn it falls due. `chooseGovernment()` discharges it. The handler is registered with the rules, so a game loaded mid-Anarchy can still finish its revolution.

`ChooseGovernment` (mandatory) is offered once the choice is due. `Revolution` is withdrawn while one is pending, which covers a zero-turn revolution (the Pyramids) where the government hasn't changed yet.
`Anarchy` is registered in the available governments, so a save taken during it can name the class. No `Availability` rule matches it, so it is never offered.

A city's citizens are its worked tiles (the centre included) plus its specialists, and there are size + 1 of them. assignWorkers, assignWorker, reassignWorkers and changeWorkedTile now count both:

working an unworked tile uses up a specialist, Entertainers first;

log: Where a tile offers more than one Move-type action, moveAlongPath now prefers an action whose class is exactly Move while the unit is only passing through, and takes the first Move-type action as before on the last tile of the route or with the unit's last move.

Only aircraft get both kinds on one tile (civ1-unit offers LandAircraft and Move on friendly cities and Carriers), so this lets a GoTo fly over them instead of landing and ending the turn, while still landing at the destination, or on a Carrier reached with the last move rather than crashing over it (civ-clone/web-renderer#82).

Move is now offered to Air units on tiles where they could land, and the land-aircraft action is registered before move so LandAircraft stays the first action there: the arrow keys and SimpleAIClient's neighbour scoring still land. A GoTo (base-unit-action-goto's moveAlongPath) and the frontend's action menu can take the plain Move to fly over instead (civ-clone/web-renderer#82).

Tests cover the action order, flying over a city and a Carrier with a plain Move, and GoTo routes through cities, ending on a Carrier, and reaching a Carrier with the last move. base-unit-action-goto is added as a devDependency for those.
aircraftCanReturn counts the player's Carriers with room as somewhere to get back to, as well as its cities.
An aircraft is deferred (setWaiting) while any of the player's Carriers that could carry it still have moves, so it plans against the Carrier's end-of-turn position.
preProcessTurn wakes the player's aircraft aboard its Carriers: Stowed never clears itself, so a landed aircraft would otherwise never fly again.
Path-following prefers a plain Move while passing through, as base-unit-action-goto's moveAlongPath does, so a path doesn't land in a city on the way (civ-clone/web-renderer#82).

carriersFor required hasCapacity(), which counts the aircraft's own weight while it is still aboard, so a full Carrier was never a return point for its own aircraft. With no city in reach every move scored -1 and the aircraft never took off. A Carrier whose cargo includes the aircraft now counts (review on civ-clone/simple-ai-client#3).

Units carried by a ship, and aircraft landed on a Carrier, are now still aboard after you save and load a game, instead of being left stranded at sea (#81).

log: The `transports` slot was classified `never` and filed with `clients` under live connections, as if it held network `Transport`s. It is the unit `TransportRegistry`: one `TransportManifest` per unit aboard a ship or Carrier. So no save carried them, and `gameForLoad` adopted the running game's registry instead of a fresh one. In-process that hid the loss behind manifests pointing at the pre-save units; after a real reload every stowed unit was aboard nothing.

It is now `state`, and `TransportManifest` (a `DataObject` from `core-unit-transport@0.1.9`) is in `CORE_ENTITIES` so a save can name it. web-renderer's `test:save` now lands a Fighter on a Carrier before saving and checks it is still aboard, and still `Stowed`, after loading.

Adds the standard workflow (Node 22, pnpm without a lock file, `--if-present` scripts); the repo had no CI. `prettier:check` passes `--check`. `registerClasses.ts` imports 15 `core-` packages that were only reachable by hoisting through `core-game`; they are now declared.

`core-save-game` discovers entities by walking `DataObject`s, and a manifest was a plain class, so no save carried one. A loaded game had every unit aboard a ship or Carrier still marked `Stowed` but aboard nothing: the ship sailed without it, and an aircraft was lost at its next fuel check. `StrategyNote` went through the same change.

It now extends `DataObject` with `sourceTile`, `transport` and `unit` as keys, all entities, so they are saved as `$ref`s and restored as the loaded instances. The constructor signature is unchanged. Hydration fills entities before registering them, so the `_byUnit`/`_byTransport` indexes key on the restored units. Declares `@civ-clone/core-data-object`.
CI now uses the standard workflow (Node 22, pnpm without a lock file, `--if-present` scripts), and `prettier:check` passes `--check`.

log: LandAircraft extends Move. After the move it empties the aircraft's moves and sets it inactive, because landing ends its turn. Given a transport (a Carrier), it also stows the aircraft aboard and marks it with Embark's Stowed busy rule, then re-processes Moved as Embark does. Without a transport (a city) nothing is stowed.

It is named LandAircraft rather than Land so it doesn't clash with the Land unit and terrain types in the ClassRegistry, DataObject ids and the data transfer's action names (civ-clone/web-renderer#81).

`civ1-unit:unit/defeated/destroy-stack` processed `Destroyed` for the defender once per stack mate instead of for each stack mate, so the rest of the stack survived. Adds civ1-unit:unit/action/land-aircraft, offering LandAircraft (from the new @civ-clone/base-unit-action-land-aircraft) when an Air unit moves onto one of its player's cities, or onto a friendly NavalTransport with capacity that canStow it. On a Carrier the aircraft is stowed and marked Stowed, so the fuel rule's transportRegistry.hasUnit check counts it as landed; in a city (also a city with a Carrier in it) it just lands. Either way its moves are emptied. The shared canLandAircraft check also removes those tiles from the Air branch of civ1-unit:unit/action/move, so LandAircraft is the only action there (civ-clone/web-renderer#81).

Taking off: Disembark sets moves to 0, which would strand a Fighter, so Air units no longer get Disembark. They take off with a plain Move, and the new civ1-unit:unit/moved/take-off rule unloads an Air unit (and clears Stowed) once it has left its transport's tile. The new civ1-unit:unit/movement-cost/transported/air rule makes the move-cargo Move free for an Air unit following its Carrier, since a landed aircraft has no moves left and would otherwise be left behind.

Each mandatory action in `takeTurn()` is now handled in its own try/catch. When handling a `Unit` throws (a rule failing inside `unit.action()` or `unit.actions()`), the error is logged with the unit's id, the unit is given `NoOrders` (or, if that throws too, has its moves zeroed and is set inactive) and the loop carries on with the player's other units. Errors from anything other than a unit still reject `takeTurn()` as before, since skipping a city build or research choice has no safe fallback.
Adds a regression test: a `Moved` rule that throws for one Warrior no longer stops a second Warrior from moving that turn.

Once a game starts, a history entry of our own catches Back and asks whether to leave; anything else that would leave the page gets the browser's own prompt. The page's own reloads (the reload shortcut, loading a save, importing assets) have already asked, so they skip it.

The player patches sent on a unit's defeat and a city's capture serialised everything but the player and its units as bare refs. A player's actions, and a unit's actions and yields, are rebuilt with fresh ids on every call, so the frontend had never been sent them: each reconstituted as `undefined`, and `mandatoryActions` holding one broke `autoEndOfTurn`. They are now sent inline.
`reconstituteData` also leaves a ref it cannot resolve out of a list, rather than handing every consumer an `undefined` hole.

`test:patch-refs` plays a seeded game through an automated `DataTransferClient`, applies what it sends the way the renderer does, and fails on any reachable ref that does not resolve. It fails without this fix, naming the same types the issue saw.
